source.notes: ICSE Grade IX school Unit Test - I in Science (school not named). Header prints 'GRADE - IX', 'UNIT TEST - I', 'SCIENCE', 'M.M:- 60'; the paper has Section A (Physics) 20 marks, Section B (Chemistry) 20 marks and Section C (Biology) 20 marks. This pack holds only Section A (Physics), so maxMarks is that section's printed 20. No year or duration is printed; examYear 2024 is taken from the file name (icse-class-9-ut1-science-030424-2024, i.e. 03-04-2024). Marks are printed per question group; where a group total covers several sub-items with no per-item marks, the group is kept as one entry with that total. The scan carries a student's ticks and some handwritten additions, which were ignored. No answer key is printed; no official answers exist.
source.usage: School examination paper published on icseboard.org (originally icseonline.com); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to where it was obtained. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text:
Choose the correct answers to the questions from the given options:
(i) Which of the following is not a contact force:
a) friction force b) force of tension c) normal reaction force d) electrostatic force
(ii) S.I. unit of momentum is:
a) kg m s⁻¹ b) g cm s⁻¹ c) kg m s d) g cm s
(iii) A force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 5 Kg. Find the acceleration.
a) 50 m s⁻² b) 2 m s⁻² c) 15 m s⁻² d) 25 m s⁻²
(iv) Action and reaction act on the:
a) same body in opposite direction b) different bodies in opposite direction c) different bodies, but in same direction d) same body, but in same direction

questions.text:
Answer the following questions: (Attempt any three)
a) Why does a ball thrown vertically upward in a moving train, come back to the thrower's hand?
b) Show that the rate of change of momentum = mass x acceleration.
c) Explain the motion of a rocket with the help of Newton's third law.
d) State Newton's law of gravitation.
e) What is the importance of the law of gravitation?

Parts (d) and (e) are on gravitation, which has no chapter in the list; 'laws-of-motion' suggested for the group

questions.text:
Numericals :-
a) A force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg for 3 s, initially at rest. Calculate : (i) the velocity acquired by the body, and (ii) change in momentum of the body.
b) A car of mass 480 kg moving at a speed of 54 km/h is stopped by applying brakes in 10 s. Calculate the force applied by the brakes.
c) A ball is released from a height and it reaches the ground in 3 s. If g= 9.8 m s⁻², find:
(a) The height from the ball was released
(b) The velocity with which the ball will strike the ground.
